careerGoal.title: A well-planned curriculum designed from scratch; Mapped to real job descriptions.
careerGoal.alt: Cohort of MBA Fintech students walking on the KRMU campus steps

courses.title: Managerial Economics
courses.desc: How do you use economic reasoning – about prices, demand, competition, and policy – to make sharper business decisions?
details: How do you tell whether a price hike will earn more revenue, or lose customers faster than the margin grows?
How do you tell which of your costs will move with volume and which will not, and price accordingly?
How do you decide what to make in-house and what to outsource, using cost-and-control logic rather than gut?
How do you read currency movement and tell whether it helps or hurts your business, and by how much?
How do you compete in a market where the marginal cost has dropped close to zero, like power at the wholesale level, content, or digital services?

courses.title: Business Analytics and Data Visualization
courses.desc: How do you go from a vague business problem to a decision-ready insight that a senior manager can actually act on?
details: How do you turn a vague business concern ('sales are down', 'customers are unhappy') into a clear question with measurable variables?
How do you turn messy operational data (CRM dumps, ERP exports, Excel files from three departments) into something you can actually analyse?
How do you decide the level of detail to hold the data at – every transaction, daily totals, or monthly summaries?
How do you tell whether two variables are causally related, correlated, or just moving together by coincidence?
How do you read a dataset and spot the trend, the anomaly, and the lurking outlier in under thirty minutes?
How do you build a dashboard a senior manager actually reads, instead of one that looks impressive and gets ignored?

courses.title: Management Theory and Practice
courses.desc: How do you build the personal philosophy, the ethical frame, and the judgement to lead well when there is no rulebook?
details: How do you tell whether a decision is ethical when 'the policy' does not cover the situation?
How do you build a personal framework for hard choices that holds up under pressure, against incentive, and over time?
How do you decide what to spend your life on, and let that choice shape the work you say yes to?
How do you read a company's actual culture from its hiring, its processes, and its structure, not from what HR says it is?
How do you turn an abstract vision into the daily decisions that actually create or destroy that culture?

courses.title: Organizational Behaviour
courses.desc: How do you read people, motivate teams, and shape workplace culture, including when you are not yet the boss?
details: How do you tell what genuinely motivates you, and keep doing the work that gives you that?
How do you give and receive feedback without it becoming about ego, defensiveness, or politics?
How do you motivate a team member who is checking out, without resorting to threats or hollow pep talks?
How do you build a team that actually performs, rather than one that just plays nice in meetings?
How do you handle a conflict on your team that is starting to leak into the work?
How do you get a cross-functional project done when you have no formal authority over any of the people involved?

courses.title: Sales & Distribution Management
courses.desc: How do you build, run, and improve a sales and distribution engine that hits the number without breaking the channel?
details: How do you set sales targets that stretch the team without setting them up to fail?
How do you sell into a large account where the buying decision involves five or more people across departments?
How do you set up a distribution network in India given the realities of GT, MT, and e-commerce living side by side?
How do you choose, deploy, and actually use a CRM so that it helps the team rather than burdening them?

courses.title: Managerial Finance
courses.desc: How do you make and defend capital decisions – where to invest, how to fund it, when to return cash – so that the business creates value rather than destroys it?
details: How do you evaluate whether a capital expenditure project will create or destroy value for the business?
How do you decide the right mix of debt and equity for a company at a given stage of its life?
How do you decide whether to return cash to shareholders (dividends, buybacks) or reinvest it?
How do you manage working capital tightly enough that the business is not asking for cash every quarter?
How do you stress-test a financial plan against realistic downside scenarios – recession, regulation, a key customer leaving?

courses.title: Human Resource Management
courses.desc: How do you find, build, and keep the team that actually does the work – as a line manager who hires them, or as an HR specialist who builds the systems they work in?
details: How do you interview a candidate so that you actually learn whether they can do the job?
How do you design a performance review system that drives improvement rather than ritual?
How do you set a compensation structure that retains your good people without breaking the budget?
How do you design an organisation – reporting lines, spans of control, decision rights – that supports the strategy?

courses.title: Legal Environment & Corporate Governance
courses.desc: How do you make business decisions that stay inside the legal and governance lines – without becoming the manager who needs a lawyer for every small choice?
details: How do you read a commercial contract well enough to know what you are committing your company to?
How do you tell whether a hiring, firing, or HR decision is legally safe in the Indian context?
How do you stay on the right side of competition law in pricing, partnerships, and market conduct?
How do you protect your company's intellectual property, and respect someone else's?
How do you stay compliant with SEBI, GST, and labour codes without burying your team in paperwork?

courses.title: Entrepreneurship & Innovation
courses.desc: How do you turn an idea into a business – yours or your employer's – that actually works in the market?
details: How do you test whether your idea has product-market fit, or whether you have just convinced yourself?
How do you find your first ten customers without a marketing budget?
How do you build a founding team where the equity split, the roles, and the trust survive the hard quarters?
How do you decide whether to bootstrap, raise angel money, or raise institutional capital?
How do you price your product when there is no comparable in the market?

courses.title: Field Challenge Studio
courses.desc: How do you take a real problem – yours, your client's, or your country's – and work it through a disciplined process into a recommendation someone can act on?
details: How do you turn a vague problem statement into a sharp question you can investigate?
How do you conduct on-ground interviews with people who do not naturally trust outsiders?
How do you observe behaviour, not just listen to claims — and spot the gap between the two?
How do you bring management frameworks to a solution design without forcing the problem into the framework?
How do you stress-test a solution against the realities of cost, capability, time, and adoption?

courses.title: Business Research Method
courses.desc: How do you talk to customers, users, and stakeholders so you actually learn what is true – not what they want you to hear, and not what you want to believe?
details: How do you get past 'would you use this?' and 'do you like this idea?' – the two most useless questions in business?
How do you ask about problems people actually have, instead of pitching solutions you already believe in?
How do you decide whom to talk to – and know when you have narrowed the segment enough that the signal becomes sharp?
How do you tell whether someone is being polite, or whether they really mean to take the action they just said they would?
How do you synthesise a series of conversations into something you can actually act on – decisions, not just notes?
